source.document: Airbus / China Eastern Airlines (CES) A319/A320/A321 Flight Crew Operating Manual, Volume 3 — Flight Operations
source.pdfPageNumbering: 1-based; not the printed section page number
source.providedBy: User-supplied PDFs; source manuals and raster pages are not included in this repository

evidence.meaning: The A320 description and 180-seat maximum carry the same MSN effectivity as these performance tables.
A320 general arrangement: length 37.57 m, span 34.1 m, conventional wing-tip fences; same MSN effectivity.
Flight-planning databases explicitly identify CFM56-5-B/P SAC. The stated 3% non-/P correction is scoped to those flight-planning tables.
SEQ170 climb/holding/descent entries specify CFM56-5-B4 and the A320 MSN group.
The technical table footers explicitly identify A320-214 CFM56-5B4/P; headers and footer effectivity were checked visually.

notes: This is one confirmed configuration in a multi-aircraft manual. CES ALL does not make a numerical table applicable to every Airbus model.
These rows do not directly apply to A319, A321, non-/P engines, sharklet variants, NEO or modified aircraft.
The numerical grid does not establish certified operating mass or altitude limits for any individual MSN.
Exact match to reference data is separate from the model's independent aerodynamic/propulsive predictions and calibration.

climb.boundary: Brake release to the selected flight level; takeoff and initial climb are included.
climb.massBasis: Weight at brake release, as printed. Cumulative entries at different FL use this same original reference mass.
climb.fuelBasis: Aircraft total. Do not multiply by engine count or add a separate takeoff allowance.

conditions.speedProfile: 250 kt from 1500 ft to FL100; accelerate 250 to 300 kt; climb at 300 kt then M0.78 to the selected altitude

sourceTables.extraction: Native 1-bit raster, column OCR with table lines removed, all rows visually checked; specific OCR repairs recorded in quality.

notes: FL15 contains takeoff and initial climb, not pure ground roll. At 60 t it is 163 kg, 2 min and 3 NM.
The difference C(m0, FL2)-C(m0, FL1) refers to the same brake-release mass m0; a later step-climb entry mass is not automatically that same reference.
Eleven genuinely empty cells remain absent: FL390 at 66–78 t, and FL370 at 72–78 t.
This first dataset extracts ISA0 only. Additional ISA+10/+15/+20 sheets exist and are catalogued; their numbers are not silently inferred.
Time and distance are integer-rounded source outputs. Very short differences can lose resolution; they are not instantaneous climb rates.
The source labels the fourth field TAS but does not define it as final cruise TAS. Preserve the printed values without that reinterpretation.
Corrections are metadata only; the lookup does not apply them automatically.

descent.boundary: Selected FL down to 1500 ft; approach and landing are not included in this pure phase table.
descent.massBasis: The source heading is WEIGHT (1000KG). The selected general and table pages do not define whether this is initial, final or mean descent mass.
descent.fuelBasis: Aircraft total; not fuel per engine.

conditions.thrust: IDLE THRUST heading; numeric N1 exceptions retained where printed

units.n1Pct: percent, or null for the source's IDLE label

correctionsPct.nullMeaning: Dash in the source correction table; no numerical correction provided here.

notes: Do not claim a descent-start or descent-end interpretation of WEIGHT from this source; callers must name their assumed reference mass explicitly.
At 45 t, FL390/370/350 give numeric N1=68.8/69.9/72.1 despite the general IDLE THRUST heading. Other cells say IDLE, stored as null rather than zero.
FL15 has zero cumulative descent time, distance and fuel. An arrival allowance belongs after this endpoint.
The 2.05.30 descent correction for integrated cruise is a different calculation and already includes a six-minute IFR arrival. Do not add it to these full phase values.

holding.boundary: Race-track holding pattern at green-dot speed, clean configuration.
holding.massBasis: Fuel planning instruction: use the landing weight at the alternate (Volume 2 PDF647). The calculation worksheet subtracts holding fuel after alternate landing weight (PDF657 lines12–14).
holding.fuelBasis: The numerical table explicitly gives FF in KG/H/ENG; multiply by engineCount and hours only at the call site.
notes: The general page discusses total holding fuel; the numerical sheet's explicit per-engine unit takes precedence for its entries.
Green dot in clean configuration and S speed in CONF1 lie between minimum-fuel and minimum-drag speed according to the general page.
Straight-line correction is not part of race-track values and is not applied automatically.

taxi.note: Includes start-up and taxi. The stated average is rounded; 11.5×12 is 138 kg.

approachAndLanding.note: Trip fuel includes descent to1500ft above destination, then approach and landing. The four-minute VFR value is stated for the alternate approach procedure.

goAround.note: Allowance included in alternate fuel; not automatically part of every trip arrival.

holdingPlanningReference.note: Explicitly described as a conservative quantity, not a replacement for the mass-dependent holding table.

contingency.note: According to national regulations and company policy, generally a percentage of trip fuel; no fixed percentage specified on this page.

integratedCruisePlanning.purpose: Catalogue of the separate whole-route integrated-cruise method. These corrections are not full phase burns and are not combined with the phase rows automatically.

nonPEngineCorrection.scope: Following flight-planning calculation tables based on CFM56-5-B/P SAC; non-/P engines only.

climbCorrection.note: Correction to fuel and time already calculated from integrated cruise over the route, not full climb fuel.

stepClimbCorrection.note: Applies to the integrated-cruise planning method. Source does not assign the exact FL290 boundary to either height.

descentCorrection.note: This fictitious integrated-cruise reference is not an explicit mass definition for the pure descent table in3.05.30.

takeoffAirportAltitudeCorrection.signInWorksheet: Added to overhead-destination weight; reduces required fuel relative to sea-level integrated reference.

quality.extraction: The main numerical content is raster. Native image OCR was used as an aid; the committed transcription was checked against rendered pages, including every row and the source headings/footnotes.

ocrRepairs.reason: OCR omitted distance71 in a line joined to another field.

limitations: The phase rows preserve raw reference semantics, including the unresolved start/end timing of descent WEIGHT.
No unprinted cells, temperature extrapolation, aircraft variant substitution or bleed corrections are synthesized.
Remaining ISA temperatures, other holding configurations and cruise numerical tables are catalogued for later extraction.
